title: Air India Picks JFK's New Terminal 6 for Operations Starting 2028
excerpt: The airline will move into the $4.2 billion terminal being built at New York's busiest international airport, upgrading the experience for travelers on one of the world's busiest India-US routes.
body:
• Air India has selected JFK Airport's new Terminal 6 for its New York operations beginning in 2028
  • Terminal 6, part of a $4.2 billion redevelopment, will replace aging infrastructure with modern gates, lounges, and seamless international connections
  • JFK's India routes are among the busiest international corridors from New York, serving hundreds of thousands of passengers annually
  • The move comes as Air India undergoes a broader transformation under Tata Group ownership, including fleet modernization and service upgrades

Air India has chosen JFK Airport's new Terminal 6 as the home for its New York operations starting in 2028, the airline announced — a move that will give one of the world's busiest India-US air corridors a significant infrastructure upgrade.

A New Terminal for a Transforming Airline

Terminal 6 is part of JFK's massive $4.2 billion redevelopment project, designed to replace aging facilities with a modern, purpose-built international terminal. The new terminal will feature expanded gates, premium lounges, improved baggage handling, and streamlined connections — a sharp contrast to the dated facilities Air India passengers have long navigated at JFK.

For Air India, the move aligns with its ongoing transformation under Tata Group ownership. Since the Tata acquisition in 2022, the airline has embarked on an ambitious overhaul: ordering hundreds of new aircraft from Airbus and Boeing, refreshing its brand identity, merging Vistara into its operations, and upgrading its product across all cabin classes.

Why JFK Matters

New York is Air India's most important US gateway. The airline operates multiple daily flights between JFK and Indian cities including Delhi and Mumbai, serving a mix of business travelers, tourists, and the massive Indian-American community concentrated in the New York metro area.

The current experience at JFK for Air India passengers has long been a point of frustration — crowded terminals, outdated infrastructure, and limited lounge options that contrast sharply with the experience offered by Gulf carriers and other international airlines operating from newer terminals.

NRI Impact

For the Indian diaspora on the US East Coast, the terminal move is more than an aviation story — it's about dignity of travel. JFK handles a significant share of the roughly 2 million annual air passengers between the US and India, and the quality of the airport experience is a perennial topic in NRI community discussions.

The 2028 timeline means the new terminal should coincide with the next phase of Air India's fleet refresh, when newer wide-body aircraft with updated cabins are expected to dominate the airline's long-haul routes. Combined, the fleet and terminal upgrades could meaningfully shift perceptions of Air India among diaspora travelers who have increasingly opted for Emirates, Qatar Airways, and other Gulf carriers.

Air India's choice of Terminal 6 also positions it alongside other international carriers that are expected to operate from the new facility, potentially improving connection options for passengers traveling beyond New York.
